items.label: f04-last-profile
items.front: What does the profile store do when asked to delete the only remaining profile version, and what if it deletes the active one?
items.back: Deleting the last version throws (create another first). Deleting the active version among several makes the first remaining profile active.

items.label: f02-promise-queue
items.front: How does performStoreOperation serialize profile reads and writes, and why is the stored queue next.catch(() => undefined)?
items.back: Each operation chains onto a module-level promise (queue.then(execute)). The caller gets the real promise, but the queue keeps a version with errors swallowed so one failed operation cannot reject - and thereby block - every later one.

items.label: f01-native-setter
items.front: Why does filler.ts write values through Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(prototype, "value").set and then dispatch input and change events?
items.back: Framework-controlled inputs (React) track value through the element's own setter; calling the prototype's native setter and dispatching bubbling, composed input/change events makes the framework notice the change instead of reverting it.

items.label: f03-longest-skill-first
items.front: For a "Years of experience with React Native" question, why are saved skills sorted by normalized length before matching?
items.back: Longer names are tried first, so "react native" wins over "react"; the match is also whole-token (bounded by non-alphanumeric characters), so a shorter skill cannot claim a longer one's question.

items.prompt: A select labeled "Are you a US citizen authorized to work in the United States?" offers Yes/No. What does the matcher do with the saved authorization answer?

choices.text: Nothing automatic - the label fails the strict affirmative-US pattern and contains "citizen", so it becomes a review item
It fills the saved legallyAuthorizedUS answer, since the options are an explicit yes/no pair
It fills Yes, because the label mentions both authorization and the United States
It skips the field as a protected credential question

choices: Nothing automatic - the label fails the strict affirmative-US pattern and contains "citizen", so it becomes a review item
It fills the saved legallyAuthorizedUS answer, since the options are an explicit yes/no pair
It fills Yes, because the label mentions both authorization and the United States
It skips the field as a protected credential question

items.explanation: Only labels matching the anchored clearAuthorization regex qualify, and any of not/without/unable/unless/except/only/citizen/citizenship forces review.

items.prompt: Two options tabs loaded the same profile at revision 4. Tab A saves successfully. Tab B then saves with expectedRevision 4. What happens to Tab B's save?

choices.text: It throws "This profile changed in another window..." - Tab A's save bumped the revision to 5, so B's expected revision no longer matches
It succeeds and overwrites Tab A's changes (last write wins)
It succeeds but marks the profile unconfigured until reviewed again
It succeeds and merges both tabs' field changes

choices: It throws "This profile changed in another window..." - Tab A's save bumped the revision to 5, so B's expected revision no longer matches
It succeeds and overwrites Tab A's changes (last write wins)
It succeeds but marks the profile unconfigured until reviewed again
It succeeds and merges both tabs' field changes

items.explanation: Every successful non-delete mutation increments revision. update compares op.expectedRevision to the stored revision before validating or writing.

items.prompt: A form has two "Company" fields, each inside its own employment-history block, and both initially map to experienceCompany. What does mapFields return for them?

choices.text: The first field gets entry zero and the second is skipped as a duplicate
Both receive the first saved employer, since entry zero is the most recent job
Both are downgraded to medium confidence with their value removed - repeated history fields need manual matching to the right profile entry
Each field receives the profile entry at the same index as its position on the page

choices: The first field gets entry zero and the second is skipped as a duplicate
Both receive the first saved employer, since entry zero is the most recent job
Both are downgraded to medium confidence with their value removed - repeated history fields need manual matching to the right profile entry
Each field receives the profile entry at the same index as its position on the page

items.explanation: mapFields counts education/experience kinds; any kind seen more than once loses its value and becomes medium. The comment says it plainly: do not silently repeat entry zero, including the first row.

items.prompt: Filling a <select> with the value "Yes": one enabled option has text "Yes", and a different enabled option has value="yes". Which option does fillField choose?

choices.text: The option whose value attribute is "yes", because machine values are more stable than labels
Neither - two candidate options make the choice ambiguous, so the fill is refused
Whichever of the two appears first in the option list
The option whose visible text is "Yes" - label matches take priority, and value matches are consulted only when no label matches

choices: The option whose value attribute is "yes", because machine values are more stable than labels
Neither - two candidate options make the choice ambiguous, so the fill is refused
Whichever of the two appears first in the option list
The option whose visible text is "Yes" - label matches take priority, and value matches are consulted only when no label matches

items.explanation: labelMatches is computed first; matches falls back to value comparison only if labelMatches is empty. Ambiguity is judged within the chosen list (exactly one match required).

items.prompt: How does AudioRecorder.start choose the recording format and how often does it ask MediaRecorder for data?

choices.text: The first supported of audio/webm;codecs=opus, audio/webm, audio/mp4, with recorder.start(1000) emitting a chunk about every second
The browser default type, with recorder.start(250) emitting four chunks per second
Always audio/mp4 for compatibility, with one blob delivered when recording stops
The first supported of audio/mp4 then audio/webm, with chunks emitted every ten seconds

choices: The first supported of audio/webm;codecs=opus, audio/webm, audio/mp4, with recorder.start(1000) emitting a chunk about every second
The browser default type, with recorder.start(250) emitting four chunks per second
Always audio/mp4 for compatibility, with one blob delivered when recording stops
The first supported of audio/mp4 then audio/webm, with chunks emitted every ten seconds

items.explanation: The mime preference list is checked with MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported; the 1000 ms timeslice is what makes per-second chunk persistence possible.

items.prompt: The scan saw an empty First name input and produced a high-confidence mapping, but the user typed into that input before the fill loop reached it. What does fillField do?

choices.text: It returns false and leaves the typed text alone - it re-checks the live element value at fill time because a scan cannot authorize replacing later typing
It overwrites the text but records the typed value in the rollback batch so Undo restores it
It overwrites the text, because the mapping was computed while the field was still empty
It appends the saved first name after the typed text

choices: It returns false and leaves the typed text alone - it re-checks the live element value at fill time because a scan cannot authorize replacing later typing
It overwrites the text but records the typed value in the rollback batch so Undo restores it
It overwrites the text, because the mapping was computed while the field was still empty
It appends the saved first name after the typed text

items.explanation: mapField already skips fields whose valueBefore is nonempty, but that is scan-time data. filler.ts checks element.value.trim() again right before writing.

items.prompt: fillField receives a mapping whose confidence is "medium" and whose value is a perfectly valid saved email. What happens?

choices.text: The value is written and recorded in the rollback batch so Undo can remove it
Nothing is written - fillField returns false for any mapping that is not high confidence, regardless of how good the value looks
The value is written only if the field is marked required on the page
The value is written but flagged in the sidebar for the user to double-check

choices: The value is written and recorded in the rollback batch so Undo can remove it
Nothing is written - fillField returns false for any mapping that is not high confidence, regardless of how good the value looks
The value is written only if the field is marked required on the page
The value is written but flagged in the sidebar for the user to double-check

items.explanation: The very first guard in fillField rejects confidence !== "high" (and empty values, disabled and read-only fields). Medium and low are review-only by design.

items.prompt: An employment Start date field is a native <input type="date">, and the saved entry starts in March 2021. What does dateMapping produce?

choices.text: A high-confidence "2021-03", the same format used for type="month" inputs
A medium-confidence review item - the profile stores month/year only, so a complete calendar date needs the user's review
A high-confidence "03/2021", the fallback month/year format
A high-confidence "2021-03-01", defaulting the day to the first of the month

choices: A high-confidence "2021-03", the same format used for type="month" inputs
A medium-confidence review item - the profile stores month/year only, so a complete calendar date needs the user's review
A high-confidence "03/2021", the fallback month/year format
A high-confidence "2021-03-01", defaulting the day to the first of the month

items.explanation: type="date" returns review before any formatting. Only type="month" gets the YYYY-MM form; dates needing a day are manual.

items.prompt: An enabled radio group labeled "Gender", with nothing selected yet, has an option exactly matching the saved EEO gender. What mapping does mapField produce?

choices.text: A high-confidence eeoGender mapping, because the saved answer exactly matches an option
A low-confidence eeoGender mapping that fills only when the field is required
A medium review item of kind unknown - checkbox and radio controls are always left for the user to select
A skip, because EEO questions are protected personal data

choices: A high-confidence eeoGender mapping, because the saved answer exactly matches an option
A low-confidence eeoGender mapping that fills only when the field is required
A medium review item of kind unknown - checkbox and radio controls are always left for the user to select
A skip, because EEO questions are protected personal data

items.explanation: The checkbox/radio check runs before the EEO table is consulted, so the exact-option EEO rule only ever applies to selects and text controls.

items.prompt: Restoring a recovery backup: which treatment do the restored profile versions receive?

choices.text: Their original IDs, but configured is forced to false
Their original IDs and revisions, so open editors keep working against them
Fresh IDs with their configured flags preserved, and no backup because the restored data replaces it
Fresh random IDs, configured=false and revision 0 - after the existing saved data is copied into profileRecoveryBackup

choices: Their original IDs, but configured is forced to false
Their original IDs and revisions, so open editors keep working against them
Fresh IDs with their configured flags preserved, and no backup because the restored data replaces it
Fresh random IDs, configured=false and revision 0 - after the existing saved data is copied into profileRecoveryBackup

items.explanation: New IDs invalidate old editors; configured=false forces review before autofill; the pre-restoration data is written to profileRecoveryBackup before profileStore is replaced.

items.prompt: The injected content script (same extension id, but its sender.url is the job site's page) sends EAM_STORE with operation action "update". How does the service worker respond?

choices.text: It performs the update, because the sender id matches the extension's own id
It refuses with "Invalid sender." because content scripts never share the extension id
It silently ignores the message and never calls sendResponse
It refuses with "Open Manage profiles to change profile data." - callers that are not extension pages may only perform get

choices: It performs the update, because the sender id matches the extension's own id
It refuses with "Invalid sender." because content scripts never share the extension id
It silently ignores the message and never calls sendResponse
It refuses with "Open Manage profiles to change profile data." - callers that are not extension pages may only perform get

items.explanation: The sender.id check passes for the content script; the second check requires sender.url to start with the extension origin for anything other than action "get".

items.prompt: After Autofill filled Email, the user edited that Email field by hand, then pressed Undo. What happens to the Email field?

choices.text: It reverts to the empty value it had before the fill
It keeps the user's edit - rollback skips any entry whose current value no longer equals the value the fill wrote
It reverts to the autofilled email, since that is the batch's last known state
Undo is refused for the whole batch because one field changed

choices: It reverts to the empty value it had before the fill
It keeps the user's edit - rollback skips any entry whose current value no longer equals the value the fill wrote
It reverts to the autofilled email, since that is the batch's last known state
Undo is refused for the whole batch because one field changed

items.explanation: rollbackFilled continues past entries where element.value !== entry.afterValue, so later manual edits survive; the other entries in the batch are still rolled back.
